A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Ab-MDP/MEAD work. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original 2D Crafting and MiniHack experiments, transfer results, learned-component evaluations and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds baseline comparisons and sensitivity analyses, including Figures 23, 25, 30, 35 and 36.

M1.justification: The discriminative transition model, count-based exploration, MCTS, Dijkstra planning and training algorithm are retained. Expanded attention-network and learned-map descriptions document existing components; the PDFs do not establish a changed MEAD procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same three 2D Crafting tasks, five MiniHack skill environments, sandbox transfer and compositional scenario. New experiments reuse this coverage. The robotics examples in v2 Table 1 are proposed applications, not evaluated domains.

E2.justification: v2 adds MuZero to the five MiniHack comparisons in Figure 4b and NCS-style k-means/greedy planning plus a k-means/Dijkstra variant in Appendix F.1.3 and Figure 23. Existing comparators remain. DAC-MDP and DLP-EIT appear in the conceptual comparison table without corresponding benchmark results.

E3.justification: Additional protocols vary encoder training fractions from 1% to 90%, fixed optimization budgets from 100 to 2500 steps, Dreamer training ratios and MuZero self-play delays. These substantially expand controlled evaluation; the original benchmark metrics and default MEAD, Dreamer and PPO settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds encoder-data sensitivity and downstream planning analysis (Figure 25), an additional fixed-budget optimization analysis (Figure 30), and Dreamer/MuZero training-setting analyses (Figures 35–36). Figure 23 also compares greedy versus Dijkstra planning with the NCS-style model. Earlier ablations remain.

E5.justification: v1 states a minimum of three independent seeds. v2 Table 6 specifies counts by main experiment and method, including four/five MEAD seeds for Crafting/MiniHack. This is additional disclosure, not evidence of increased runs. Existing confidence-interval and stated exception conventions are retained.

E6.justification: New MuZero, NCS and sensitivity results materially expand the evidence. v2 Figure 23 shows the k-means/Dijkstra variant failing four-step Crafting but learning in Freeze-Wand; Figure 25 shows poor planning with very small encoder datasets. Retained main mean curves are unchanged, although some confidence bands differ slightly.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.1.3 supplies mathematical correspondences between Ab-MDP and OO-MDP, NCS and DLP representations, including a comparison of transition-dependency assumptions. The existing Ab-MDP definitions, Remark B.3 and single-/multi-item counterexample analysis remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and discussion retain the claims about abstraction, discriminative world modelling, sample efficiency, transfer, planning and learning abstraction components. Additional comparisons support these claims without materially redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix B.1.3 adds explanations of attention-mediated object interactions and the restrictions of NCS-style dynamics; B.1.4 develops possible robotics applications. The existing limitations concerning labelled object mappings and failures of single-item planning are retained.

D1.justification: v2 expands the attention architecture description and documents the learned encoder's observation/action inputs, convolutional encoder, output heads, loss, batch size and learning rate. Appendix G.3 adds MuZero's implementation source, search ranges and selected settings. These address substantial implementation gaps in v1.

R1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B.1.3 substantially expand positioning against object-centric research, including NCS, DLP-based methods and CEE-US. Table 5 compares representation, function approximation and planning choices. Additional MuZero and robotics references extend this substantive comparison beyond bibliographic restyling.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main-section/Appendix A–G organization are retained. v2 makes local wording corrections, expands explanations, introduces targeted appendix subsections and consolidates the semantic-embedding headings, without extensively rewriting the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds five experimental figures and four tables, expands Figure 14 into three environment panels, and revises Figure 4's comparator display and Figure 11's labels. It also changes title/heading styling and introduces running headers throughout. Most earlier graphics remain, often relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation by adding online-planning and object-structured comparators missing from v1, including a control separating model choice from planning choice. Encoder-data and training-budget analyses better expose performance dependencies, while fuller implementation and seed reporting improve reproducibility. These gains address important comparison and documentation gaps; the dependence on supplied or supervised abstractions remains.
